headline: Oil Slips and Chips Soar Into Tuesday's Open as Iran Tensions Ease
body_html:
Stocks arrive at Tuesday's open with the tailwind of a lopsided Monday and a calmer tone overseas. Asian shares climbed overnight as falling oil prices lifted sentiment. President Trump signaled that US military action against Iran is not necessary at this point and said Qatar and Saudi Arabia favor a peaceful outcome, though he added that the US is ready to strike if needed.

Monday's completed session was broad and decisive: 581 of the 668 stocks we track rose, while 85 fell. Semiconductors led the sectors with a 7.67% gain, followed by financials at 5.84% and industrials at 4.31%. Energy trailed at 0.64%. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor jumped 23.55%, with Coherent up 16.79% and Monolithic Power up 16.6%. On the downside, Acadia Pharmaceuticals dropped 22.28% and Hims & Hers Health lost 11.77%.

At the open, watch whether oil keeps sliding and the Iran rhetoric holds, after a Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi missiles fired toward Riyadh. Also in focus: a House impeachment vote expected this week for Pentagon chief Hegseth, and whether chip leadership can extend after such a sharp run. Pre-market prices are thin, so treat early moves with caution.

briefs.headline: Oil retreats as Washington plays down escalation
briefs.body: Crude fell after Trump said military action against Iran isn't needed right now and that Gulf states prefer a peaceful settlement. Traders will look for confirmation that the softer tone survives the day, since energy was the weakest sector in Monday's session at 0.64%.

briefs.headline: OPEC output climbs back toward pre-war levels
briefs.body: A Reuters survey showed OPEC production rose in October to roughly 90% of its pre-war rate. Returning supply helps explain the pressure on oil prices and gives energy investors another variable to weigh alongside the diplomatic headlines out of the Gulf.

briefs.headline: Boeing to shrink commercial workforce by 5%
briefs.body: The planemaker will cut about 5% of its commercial airplane workforce, saying production is ramping more slowly than it expected. The move suggests a more cautious path for output, and it is a name industrial investors will be watching at the open.

briefs.headline: Children's Place seeks protection from creditors
briefs.body: The children's apparel retailer filed for bankruptcy protection and is looking for a buyer. The filing adds to the strain on brick-and-mortar specialty retail, even as consumer shares in our universe gained 2.86% on average in Monday's session.

briefs.headline: Software names lag in a roaring market
briefs.body: While most sectors surged Monday, several software and web-platform stocks went the other way. monday.com fell 9.1%, Wix.com dropped 8.33% and LegalZoom slid 7.35%. Software as a whole still gained 2.08%, so the weakness was stock-specific.

briefs.headline: France points finger at Iran over appliance hacks
briefs.body: French officials blame Iran for a wave of hacks on household refrigerators and have vowed retaliation, according to Reuters. The story adds a cyber dimension to the Iran tensions already driving oil and sentiment, and is worth tracking for any escalation.
